researcher_notes: Kaliningrad FSRU commissioned Jan 2019 (operating, order 1) and then 'has not seen commercial activity beyond its commissioning cargo' / 'received no deliveries after arriving laden'; the vessel was diverted to conventional LNG-carrier duty (2019-2021), reinstalled at Kaliningrad in early 2022, then repurposed as a ship-to-ship export tanker for Portovaya LNG (~2022); reporting describes it as 'remains idle' as of June 2023 through 2025. No independent source pins a specific idle-START year for the terminal milestone: plausible candidates are 2019 (idle immediately after the single commissioning cargo) or 2022 (repurposed as export tanker once Portovaya LNG came online). No URL verified to a specific year; web session limit hit before resolution, so left UNRESOLVED rather than stage with doubt.

Alltech leader Dmitry Bosov reportedly said a final investment decision was planned for late 2011 (with tenders in 2012 and plant start in 2015), per Barents Observer's 'Pechora LNG from year 2015' article — but that source URL now returns 404 and could not be independently re-verified through the url_verifier. The project changed hands (Rosneft acquired 51% in 2015) implying a later expected-FID window, and it never reached FID before being abandoned in Sept 2018. With no live URL passing verification for any specific planned-FID year, left UNRESOLVED (best lead: planned FID late 2011, Alltech era). Web session limit hit before a verifiable second source could be found.

On 16 Sep 2022 Gazprom announced plans to add an additional (third) liquefaction train of up to 2 MTPA at Portovaya using domestic technology; the verified LNG Prime article (pub. 16 Sep 2022) relays Gazprom's official statement and ties the proposal to 2022. Year 2022 is well-attested across coverage, but only one URL was verified before the web session limit hit, so tier=medium (single strong source relaying the sponsor announcement; second independent corroboration not completed). The Wikipedia 'LNG industry in Russia' page mentions the planned third train but gives no year for it (its '2022' refers to plant startup), so it was deliberately not cited to avoid a misleading year-tie.

Gazprom and Shell signed a memorandum-roadmap in Feb 2014 (Sochi) to add a third LNG production train to the Sakhalin II / Prigorodnoye plant, with FEED to follow and first shipment then targeted for 2019 — the first concrete public proposal/announcement of the Train 3 expansion. Two independent verified sources (offshore-energy.biz independent media + EuropaWire carrying the official Gazprom/Shell release). Earlier informal 'examining the possibility of a third train' discussions date to the mid-2000s, but the formal proposal/roadmap milestone is Feb 2014.

Shtokman was effectively abandoned in 2012: the Gazprom/Total/Statoil shareholders' agreement expired 30 Jun 2012 without development; Statoil exited and wrote off ~$335-336m of its stake (Aug 2012); Gazprom put the project on indefinite hold (Aug 2012, FID postponed to at least 2014). It remains dead and is treated as cancelled. Three independent verified sources (Bellona, The Barents Observer, Wikipedia Shtokman field). Caveat on GEM substatus 'inferred 4 y': there was no formal sponsor 'cancellation' announcement, so if GEM applies its inferred-4-years-of-no-activity convention literally the recorded year could be ~2016 (4y after the 2012 freeze); however the best-documented effective abandonment/termination year is 2012, which is what is filled here.
